ei.title: 사후 정보 제시에서의 정보 생략과 기억 억제
ei.subject: 수능특강Light

fullPassage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing revealed that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a particular scene was omitted from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation.

(A) Subsequent testing revealed that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing.

(B) Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added.

(C) The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it.

det.korean: (B) 아이들의 취약성 + 실험 설계 → (C) 과제 지시 → (A) 테스트 결과.
det.analysis:
✅ ② (B)-(C)-(A): 도입문(정보 생략으로 인출 억제 가능) → (B) 아이들이 취약하며 Wright 등이 비디오 실험 설계 → (C) 아이들에게 상상/이야기 과제 지시 → (A) 후속 테스트 결과(생략 장면 회상 실패).

❌ ① (A)-(B)-(C): 테스트 결과가 실험 설계보다 먼저 올 수 없음.

❌ ③ (C)-(A)-(B): 과제 지시가 실험 설명 없이 먼저 올 수 없음.

❌ ④ (B)-(A)-(C): 비디오 재시청 후 바로 테스트 결과가 오면 과제 지시가 빠짐.
det.tip: 실험 순서: 설계(B) → 과제(C) → 결과(A). The children(C)이 (B)의 children을 받음.

questions.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a particular scene was omitted from a post-event interview.

det.korean: ④번 위치가 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ④: Wright 실험 결과(③번 뒤) 이후, Williams 등의 유사 효과 언급이 자연스러움. 바로 다음 'Their participants'가 Williams 등을 지칭.

❌ ①: 연구 소개 직후에 다른 연구자 결과가 오면 Wright 실험이 빠짐.

❌ ②: 비디오 재시청 후 바로 다른 연구 결과가 오면 Wright 실험 과제와 결과가 빠짐.

❌ ③: 과제 지시 후 바로 다른 연구 결과가 오면 Wright 실험 결과가 빠짐.
det.tip: Their participants(다음 문장)의 Their가 삽입 문장의 Williams, Wright and Freeman을 가리킴.

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly ①<u>susceptible</u> to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video ②<u>depicted</u> a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing ③<u>revealed</u> that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who ④<u>received</u> no second viewing. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② depicted → depicting: 'a video depicting a series of events'에서 video를 수식하는 현재분사.
det.analysis:
✅ ① susceptible: be susceptible to(~에 취약한) — 형용사 보어, 적절.

❌ ② depicted → depicting: 'a video depicting a series of events'에서 video가 사건을 능동적으로 '묘사하는' 것이므로 현재분사 depicting이 올바름. depicted(과거분사)는 수동의 의미로 부적절.

✅ ③ revealed: Subsequent testing(주어)에 대한 과거형 동사 — 적절.

✅ ④ received: 관계대명사 who 절의 동사. controls가 두 번째 시청을 '받지 않은' — 적절.
det.tip: 현재분사(능동) vs 과거분사(수동). video가 묘사하는 주체이므로 depicting(능동).

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by ①<u>omitting</u> it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing revealed that the children often ②<u>failed</u> to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made ③<u>well</u> by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a particular scene was omitted from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more ④<u>likely</u> to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ well → better: 'was actually made better'에서 비교급 better 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① omitting: by + 동명사(~함으로써) — 적절.

✅ ② failed: 'often failed to recall'에서 과거형 동사 — 적절.

❌ ③ well → better: 원문 'was actually made better'. 'compared with controls'와 함께 비교급이 필요. well의 비교급은 better.

✅ ④ likely: 'were far more likely to forget' — 비교급 구문에서 형용사 likely, 적절.
det.tip: well → better → best. 비교 대상(compared with controls)이 있으므로 비교급 better 필수.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사후 면담(a post-event interview).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ a post-event interview: Williams 등이 '사후 면담'에서 특정 장면 언급을 생략했을 때 유사한 효과 발견. 다음 문장에서도 'post-event interview' 반복.

❌ ① a subsequent video presentation: Wright 실험의 방법이지 Williams 실험이 아님.

❌ ② the original experiment: '원래 실험'은 구체적이지 않음.

❌ ④ the children's memory test: '기억 테스트'는 결과 측정이지 생략 대상이 아님.
det.tip: Williams 실험 = post-event interview(사후 면담)에서 정보 생략. Wright 실험 = 비디오 재시청.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 특정 정보의 기억 인출을 억제하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information: 사후 제시에서 생략하여 특정 정보의 '기억 인출을 억제'하는 것이 글의 핵심 주장.

❌ ② enhance children's ability to recall past events: 기억력 향상이 아니라 억제.

❌ ③ improve the accuracy of eyewitness testimony: 목격자 증언 정확도 향상은 원문 주제가 아님.

❌ ④ strengthen the formation of long-term memories: 장기 기억 형성 강화는 원문과 반대.
det.tip: inhibit the retrieval(인출 억제) = 글 전체의 핵심 주제문.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사후 정보 제시에서의 생략이 아동의 기억 인출에 미치는 억제 효과.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ the suppressive effect of information omission on children's memory retrieval: 사후 제시에서 정보 생략이 기억 인출을 억제하며 특히 아동에게 두드러짐.

❌ ① methods for improving children's eyewitness reliability: 목격자 신뢰성 향상 방법이 아님.

❌ ② the role of repetition in strengthening long-term memory: 반복의 역할이 아닌 생략의 역할.

❌ ③ developmental differences in susceptibility to memory distortion: 발달 차이가 아닌 생략 효과 자체가 주제.
det.tip: 핵심 키워드: inhibit + retrieval + omitting + susceptible + children.

the role of repetition in strengthening long-term memory
developmental differences in susceptibility to memory distortion
the suppressive effect of information omission on children's memory retrieval

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 아이들은 성인보다 사후 정보 생략에 의한 기억 억제 효과에 더 잘 영향받는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ Post-event information omission is especially effective at suppressing memory retrieval in children compared to other age groups: 'particularly susceptible'는 다른 집단보다 아이들이 이 효과에 더 취약하다는 함축.

❌ ① Children cannot remember anything if they are not shown it multiple times: '전혀 기억 못 한다'는 과장. susceptible ≠ incapable.

❌ ② Young children are generally poor at forming memories of events they witness: 일반적 기억력 저하가 아닌 특정 효과에 대한 취약성.

❌ ④ Adults are completely unaffected by the omission of information from post-event presentations: '완전히 영향받지 않는다'는 원문에 없는 주장.
det.tip: particularly susceptible = 특히 취약한. 비교 대상(다른 연령대)이 함축됨.

Young children are generally poor at forming memories of events they witness.
Post-event information omission is especially effective at suppressing memory retrieval in children compared to other age groups.
Adults are completely unaffected by the omission of information from post-event presentations.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>it</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: it = a scene(장면).
det.analysis:
✅ ① 장면(a scene): 'forget a scene if it was omitted'에서 it은 바로 앞의 a scene을 지칭. 장면이 사후 면담에서 생략되면 잊을 가능성이 높다.

❌ ② 사후 면담(the post-event interview): 면담 자체가 생략되는 것이 아님.

❌ ③ 유사한 효과(the similar effect): 효과가 생략되는 것이 아님.

❌ ④ 특정 정보(a particular piece of information): 앞 문장이 아닌 글 첫 부분의 표현으로 거리가 멂.
det.tip: 대명사 it은 같은 절 내의 직접 선행사를 가리킴. forget a scene if it was omitted → it = a scene.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 비디오에 음주운전 사건과 같은 일련의 사건이 묘사되어 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 실험 비디오에는 음주운전 사건 같은 일련의 사건이 묘사되었다: 원문 'a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident)'와 일치.

❌ ① 첫 번째 연구에서 5~6세 아이들을 대상으로 실험했다: Wright 등은 9~10세.

❌ ③ 통제 집단은 비디오를 두 번 시청했다: 통제 집단은 두 번째 시청 없음(no second viewing).

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing revealed that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a particular scene was omitted from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.
